_README: Two separate things live here, and the distinction matters.
'catalog' holds INTERNAL geometry (ball count, ball diameter, pitch
diameter) that is published and widely cross-checked. Entries here are
diameter, width) only. These are standardised across manufacturers, but
they do NOT tell you the ball count or ball diameter. bearing.py derives
those with an empirical estimator and returns confidence 0.6 with an
Deliberately NOT done: filling 'catalog' with plausible-looking internal
geometry for bearings whose real values are not published here. A wrong
ball count shifts BPFO by ~11% and the bot would state it with full
confidence. An estimate that admits it is an estimate is strictly better.
To add a bearing properly: take n_balls / ball_dia_mm / pitch_dia_mm from
the manufacturer's engineering drawing or an analyser's bearing database,
put it in 'catalog', and cite the source in 'note'.

6203.note: SKF 6203-2RS JEM. Widely published in bearing-diagnostics literature (CWRU fan-end test bearing).

6205.note: SKF 6205-2RS JEM. The de-facto reference bearing in the fault-diagnosis literature (CWRU drive-end test bearing).

boundary_dimensions._comment: series -> bore_code -> [bore_mm, outside_dia_mm, width_mm]. ISO 15 standard boundary dimensions.
